resources.string: Turn on Use from your computer
Settings › Linux workspace, which shows its address
In a terminal on this computer; leave it running.
Read it from the phone with this, then paste it here.
This computer has no key yet. Make one in Terminal, then check again:
The phone may have gone to sleep. Connect again.
Tap + by Computers, then paste its key
Add this computer's key on the phone, below.
Check the address, and that Use from your computer is on.
That isn't the phone this computer knew
If you reset Linux on the phone, remove its line from ~/.ssh/known_hosts, then connect.
Whittle uses the computer's own ssh to reach the phone.
The phone didn't accept that token
Copy it again with the command in step 3; it changes when Linux is reset.
Check that Use from your computer is on and the tunnel in step 2 is still running.
The tunnel may have closed, or the phone went to sleep. Open the tunnel again and connect.
Opens http://127.0.0.1:%1$d in this computer's browser. The server runs on your phone, so its port needs a tunnel too, in a terminal here: %2$s
Opening a tunnel to port %1$d on your phone…
Couldn't open a tunnel to port %1$d. Check that your phone is still connected, or open one in a terminal: %2$s
It isn't serving yet; try again once its card says it's live.
Phone features, the assistant and updates are in Whittle on your phone.
